fort_room.label: Ananthan Pillai's lamplit room in the Travancore fort
fort_room.anchor: A small room inside the red laterite Travancore fort: lime-washed laterite walls, a dark timber ceiling and a closed wooden shutter. Nagoji sits cross-legged on a woven mat at a low writing table stacked with string-bound palm-leaf bundles, a single clay oil lamp with an open wick beside them.
fort_room.absent: No chair, desk, paper books, quill pens, glass lamp or European furniture; no turban on Nagoji.
fort_room.time: night, a single open-wick oil lamp

border_temple.label: Village temple near the Velinadu border
border_temple.anchor: A village temple near the Velinadu border among coconut palms: low laterite plinth, a sloping two-tiered tiled Kerala roof on timber posts, a tall brass lamp-pillar in the open courtyard, offering stones and a stepped temple tank beside the path. Women in white carry brass lamps in procession with chenda drummers behind them, and everyone inside the precinct is barefoot.
border_temple.absent: No tall stone gateway tower, chairs, benches or glass lanterns, no soldiers or European figures, and no tali on Revathi.
border_temple.time: dusk, brass lamps lit along the procession

village_edge.label: Edge of the festival village at dusk
village_edge.anchor: The last houses of the festival village where a red earth road leaves between coconut palms and paddy: low laterite walls, tiled and thatched roofs, villagers carrying brass lamps home behind. Revathi's small mounted escort of Velinadu retainers in white waits in the road beside her horse.
village_edge.absent: No carriage, cart, glass lanterns or soldiers in coats; Revathi wears no tali.
village_edge.time: the third evening, dusk turning blue, the last festival lamps behind

padmini_yard.label: Padmini Amma's yard under the jackfruit tree
padmini_yard.anchor: Padmini's Travancore estate yard: a great jackfruit tree shading packed red earth, the laterite walls and sloping tiled roof of her house behind, the kalari glimpsed across the yard.
padmini_yard.absent: No chairs or benches, no fort walls, no glass lamps; Revathi wears no tali.

velinadu_gate.label: Velinadu house gate and outer compound
velinadu_gate.anchor: The Velinadu house compound: thick, newly heightened red laterite outer walls broken by a timber gatehouse under a small sloping tiled roof, a packed red earth road before it. Retainers in white mundu stand at the gate with matchlock muskets where there used to be only spears, children play in the courtyards beyond, and coconut palms rise behind the tiled roofs of the house.
velinadu_gate.absent: Not a fort: no bastions, cannon, crenellations or flags; no European buildings, uniforms, glass lanterns or stone gateway tower.
velinadu_gate.time: late afternoon, a pale full moon rising over the palms

velinadu_verandah.label: Long verandah of the Velinadu house
velinadu_verandah.anchor: The long verandah along the inner courtyard of the Velinadu house: a raised laterite plinth, polished dark floor, turned timber pillars and a carved wooden beam under deep sloping tiled eaves. Across the open courtyard boys practise with sticks in a sunken kalari pit while their sisters watch, and household women pound grain with long pestles.
velinadu_verandah.absent: No chairs, benches or European furniture, no glass lanterns, no soldiers in coats; Revathi wears no tali.
velinadu_verandah.time: late afternoon, the low sun laying the long shadows of the pillars across the floor

council_room.label: Velinadu council room off the verandah
council_room.anchor: The stretch of verandah outside the Velinadu council room and the room itself, entered through a heavy timber door: carved wooden lattice windows, a polished floor laid with the elders' empty woven mats in two rows, and the matriarch's low carved wooden seat at their head. A retainer in white mundu with a matchlock musket stands guard at the door.
council_room.absent: No throne, chairs, tables or European furniture, no elders present, no glass lamps; Revathi wears no tali.
council_room.time: late afternoon turned gold, light falling through the lattice

courtyard_steps.label: Velinadu inner courtyard at lamp-lighting
courtyard_steps.anchor: The broad laterite steps down into the Velinadu inner courtyard, ringed by tiled roofs and timber verandahs: grandmothers on a raised platform, young women at the grain, a girl touching a flame to a tall brass lamp, girls watching the kalari, a small child on a hip. Women are at the centre of everything.
courtyard_steps.absent: No chairs or benches, glass lanterns, European objects or soldiers; Revathi wears no tali.
courtyard_steps.time: lamp-lighting at dusk, violet sky above the roofs, warm brass lamplight rising on faces

stable_rail.label: Outer stable rail of the Velinadu house
stable_rail.anchor: The outer stable of the Velinadu house: a long timber rail before an open-fronted, tiled stable shed with straw underfoot and laterite walls behind, Kayal tied at the rail. A brass oil lamp with open wicks hangs from a post and gives the scene its warm light.
stable_rail.absent: No glass lantern or chimney lamp, no carriage, no European saddlery; Revathi wears no tali.
stable_rail.time: dusk deepening toward dark, lit by the hanging brass lamp

children_vision.label: Imagined children in the Velinadu courtyard
children_vision.anchor: An imagined bright day in the Velinadu inner courtyard and kalari yard: sun-warmed stones, the sunken kalari pit, tiled verandahs and small barefoot children.
children_vision.absent: No clean flashback border, no weapons, no named child and no adult other than those the description names.

verandah_moonlit.label: Velinadu verandah under the carved beam by moonlight
verandah_moonlit.anchor: The same long verandah of the Velinadu house, under the carved wooden beam where Revathi first greeted Nagoji: turned timber pillars, deep tiled eaves and the open inner courtyard beyond, silvered by the full moon. A few brass oil lamps burn low along the verandah.
verandah_moonlit.absent: No chairs or benches, glass lanterns or European objects; Revathi wears no tali.
verandah_moonlit.time: night, the full moon high over the courtyard

wedding_prep.label: Velinadu courtyard on the wedding morning
wedding_prep.anchor: The Velinadu inner courtyard being readied for the wedding: jasmine garlands and strings of mango leaves being hung between the timber pillars, brass vessels and lamps being polished, chenda and thimila drummers tuning under the tiled eaves, house elders overseeing. A household affair with no courtiers.
wedding_prep.absent: No courtiers, king, soldiers in coats, chairs, canopy or glass lamps.

wedding_fire.label: Velinadu courtyard at the wedding fire
wedding_fire.anchor: The Velinadu inner courtyard at the wedding: a small sacred fire on a low brick fire altar on the swept ground, brass lamps and vessels, jasmine garlands and mango-leaf strings under the tiled eaves. The priest sits on the far side of the fire facing the couple; Revathi sits before the fire on the near side with Nagoji kneeling at her right, the few guests stand at the back of the courtyard and the household women and elders line the sides.
wedding_fire.absent: No chairs, canopy, throne, courtiers or king, no glass lamps; no knife at Nagoji's waist, no gold border on his white wedding cloth, and no tali on Revathi's neck before the knots are tied.
wedding_fire.time: sunset, the sun touching the tops of the coconut palms, firelight on faces

memory_strip.label: Wordless memory strip during the knots
memory_strip.anchor: Three remembered images flowing into one another across a narrow strip: a young man's thin hand going under a black storm wave at night, the pale puckered brand on the inner LEFT forearm a hand's width above the wrist beside a long thin white scar, and a brass oil lamp standing on the earthen floor of a low cellar.
memory_strip.absent: No ship, deck, chains or faces; the brand shows no letters, numerals or cross; no blood.
memory_strip.time: storm dark giving way to dim cellar lamplight

wedding_celebration.label: Velinadu courtyard just after the tali is tied
wedding_celebration.anchor: The same wedding courtyard moments after the third knot: drums loud and triumphant, women ululating, guests on their feet, and at the centre the couple still seated by the fire looking only at each other. The tali now hangs high at Revathi's throat, a small gold pendant on a yellow thread separate from the longer flat-coin necklace.
wedding_celebration.absent: No chairs, canopy, courtiers or king, no glass lamps; no knife at Nagoji's waist and no gold border on his white wedding cloth.
wedding_celebration.time: dusk after sunset, firelight and brass lamps

feast.label: Wedding feast in the Velinadu courtyard
feast.anchor: A wedding feast on the Velinadu courtyard floor: rows of banana leaves laid on the ground, rice in small mountains with curries around it, pappadam, pickled mango and brass vessels of avial arriving in steam. Everyone sits cross-legged on the floor or low mats and eats with the right hand: Nagoji at his leaf with Revathi on his right, tali at her throat, Padmini on his left and Ramayyan across the row.
feast.absent: No tables, chairs, benches, plates, cutlery or glass lamps; no knife at Nagoji's waist.
feast.time: evening, brass oil lamps along the rows of leaves

western_verandah_night.label: Western verandah of the Velinadu house at night
western_verandah_night.anchor: The western verandah of the Velinadu house at night, looking out over the darkened courtyard where a few lamps burn; behind it an open door shows the house shrine, a small bronze Bhagavathi in a wall niche and a tiered brass lamp with steady flames. Both are still in their wedding clothes: Nagoji in plain white with no gold border, Revathi in indigo with her heaviest gold border, braid pinned up with jasmine, the tali at her throat.
western_verandah_night.absent: No temple building, large idol, chairs or glass lamps; no knife at Nagoji's waist.
western_verandah_night.time: night, steady brass lamplight from the shrine and a few courtyard lamps

revathi_room.label: Revathi's room on the wedding night
revathi_room.anchor: Revathi's room in the Velinadu house behind a heavy carved teak door: a single brass oil lamp on its stand, a low bed spread with white cloth and strewn with jasmine, a wooden stand for jewellery and a window with a carved timber lattice. The tali never leaves her throat, and in bed the white cloth stays drawn up to both their shoulders.
revathi_room.absent: No nudity, bare ribs or bare chest in bed, no cellar, no canopied or European bed, no glass lamps and no weapon near the bed.
revathi_room.time: night, a single open-wick brass lamp

velinadu_morning_view.label: Velinadu from above in the morning
velinadu_morning_view.anchor: A high view over the Velinadu house: tiled roofs around the inner courtyard, kitchen smoke rising, courtyards filling with the household, the kalari waking, the thick laterite outer walls and beyond them a road running away through the coconut palms.
velinadu_morning_view.absent: No foreground observer or identifiable principal; no bastions, cannon, flags, European buildings or soldiers in coats.
velinadu_morning_view.time: early morning, soft gold light and haze

western_verandah_morning.label: Western verandah of the Velinadu house in the morning
western_verandah_morning.anchor: The western verandah of the Velinadu house in morning light, looking out past the courtyard to the outer laterite walls and the road through the palms. Nagoji's waist is empty, and the tali hangs at Revathi's throat, separate from the flat-coin necklace.
western_verandah_morning.absent: No knife or sheath at Nagoji's waist, no turban on Nagoji, no chairs or glass lamps.

page-01-panel-05.time: early morning, clear sky over the temple roof and the coconut palms

page-02-panel-05.lettering_space: Leave a quiet plain band of the green cloth beside the abstract stitching for the stitched-style caption, and clear space above the palms for the two plain captions.

page-04-panel-05.bleed: Behind Revathi's present face, dry brown Deccan hills and a dust road running north bleed in from the panel edge like a stain, not a clean flashback frame. Nagoji appears only as the lone rider going away up that road, small and seen from behind.

page-08-panel-05.bleed: A warm, soft-edged picture in Nagoji's mind, its edges dissolving rather than framed: small bare feet running on the courtyard stones, a child's hand sticky with fruit tugging his hand toward the kalari, and Revathi in the background with one finger raised, scolding.

page-09-panel-02.bleed: This whole panel is Revathi's telling of a recent scene, soft-edged and warmer than the moonlit verandah, never a clean flashback frame; Revathi is exactly her present age and dress, not younger.

page-10-panel-05.time: the wedding morning, clear early light

page-13-panel-02.bleed: Memory only: the three images bleed into each other like stains with no borders between them, darker and more desaturated than the firelit ceremony around them.

page-17-panel-02.time: later in the night, the lamp out, moonlight through the window lattice

page-17-panel-03.time: later in the night, the lamp out, moonlight through the window lattice

page-17-panel-05.time: dawn light through the lattice, shadows of passing feet under the door

page-18-panel-04.bleed: A soft-edged picture of what is to come, dissolving at its edges rather than framed: unnamed children running the courtyard stones and one small rider on a pony in the kalari yard, with no adult principal in view.

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache; clean-shaven chin and jaw, smooth skin, no beard or facial scar, and a tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. Kerala topknot high on the crown, never a turban, first grey at the temples, silver chain of office and the brand only on the inner LEFT forearm; the ivory-handled conch knife is at his waist on pages 1 to 9 and in the first two panels of page 10 only, and for the wedding on pages 11 to 14 he wears a fresh plain white mundu and shoulder cloth with no gold border.
character_notes.revathi: A little younger than Nagoji: indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, a sandalwood line at the front hairline and the same few grey threads all chapter, never more. No tali on pages 1 to 11 or before the third knot on page 12; from page 12 panel 5 onward the tali is a small gold pendant on a yellow thread worn high at the throat, clearly separate from the longer flat-coin necklace, and at the wedding her braid is coiled and pinned up at the back of her head with jasmine, the nape bare.
character_notes.padmini: In her fifties: thick black hair coiled at the nape with grey threading through it, simple gold, the old Kerala sari drape hitched for walking with no stitched blouse, and a long walking stick. At the wedding and the feast she wears her finest white with jasmine in her coiled hair.
character_notes.dhanaji: Stockier and a little shorter than Nagoji, short black beard, white Maratha pagdi turban, indigo quilted tunic to the knee with long sleeves to the wrist, cream trousers, riding boots and a plain leather sword belt with his talwar, no sash, whatever the sheet shows of rolled sleeves or shoes. Never a rust-red turban, never bare-headed and never a topknot; once he takes the conch knife it stays hidden in his belt under the tunic hem.
character_notes.eustachius: Tall, pale hair tied back with a dark ribbon, no wig and no hat; a plain white cotton tunic-coat over a white ankle-length mundu with sandals, his sword hilt wrapped in local cloth, and no blue anywhere.
character_notes.ponnan: Broad-shouldered Maravar with curly hair worn loose, no topknot or turban, a thick moustache and clean chin; red shoulder cloth, short jacket and white mundu hitched to the bare knees.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin sharp features and receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead marks or sacred thread; never the officiating priest's face.
character_notes.temple_priest: Clean-shaven, curly hair in a low knot, ash lines and a red dot on the forehead, sacred thread across a bare chest, white mundu and gold-bordered shoulder cloth. He always sits on the far side of the fire facing the couple and never shares Nagoji's moustache, topknot or plain white cloth.
character_notes.kayal: Nagoji's bay mare: ochre red-brown coat with black mane, tail and lower legs, no white markings, mid-sized between a heavy charger and a pony.
character_notes.keshavrao: About nineteen, narrow shoulders, black hair hacked short, grey-brown prisoner tunic and no ear stud; in this chapter he is only a thin young hand going under a black storm wave, never a face.
